author: sonnet

changes: Added resync_pending to download_status, with a one-line definition, so a needed resync is remembered when Wi-Fi is off (Q7).
Step 4: first rule now starts step 5 for resync_pending or a first install, says what happens with no Wi-Fi, and lists ready_to_swap as in progress.
Replaced the differing step 6 and step 9 write rules with one apply rule (greater than or equal), defined once in the summary and used in steps 6, 9 and 10 (Q3).
Core idea: added why replaying page-held edits is safe, and how deletes before and after the page read are covered (Q2, Q4).
Step 6: the transaction that saves the last page also sets draining, so step 8 can pick the next step from the status alone (Q8).
Shared rule and step 9: fixed the contradiction between stopped_error and draining on a drain give-up (Q8).
Step 8: made the decision explicit, covers ready_to_swap, and states that a drain needs no Wi-Fi check (Q5, Q8).
Steps 5, 11 and 12: use resync_pending instead of status none, and a low-disk resync stays resync_pending.
Added an open item that the change_seq commit-order guarantee is relied on but unverified (Q1).
Step 8 rule 1: added the reason for the 6-day limit (one-day margin before the 7-day 410) (Q9).
Step 6 failure: stated that a persistent 4xx costs one request per trigger with no lockout (Q10).
Step 4: defined when the in-memory sync running flag is set and cleared, and that it is never stored (Q11).

POST /sync/begin now also returns approx_total; added download_approx_total to sync_state; step 5 stores it; step 1 notes it can come from table statistics; the open question uses it for progress (Q12).
Step 4: stated that a first install goes to step 5 automatically at launch when Wi-Fi is on, and that step 5 sets download_status to running (Q13).

Core idea and step 9: stated that the drain starts only after all pages are saved, how feed changes for missing products are handled, and that edits after the drain end are fetched by step 10 (Q14, Q15, Q16).
Core idea: added a paragraph saying edited products are not refetched by the page endpoint and what reps see meanwhile (Q16).
State table and step 9 item 5: said live_cursor_seq is null until the first swap, which sets it (Q17).
Step 9 item 6 and two-generation paragraph: made old-generation cleanup explicitly housekeeping that step 5 supersedes (Q18).
Step 5: said why emptying download_gen is always safe and that download_gen is 0 when active_gen is none (Q19).
Step 9 failure: noted the swap transaction leaves no intermediate state (Q19).

Reordered into the skill layout: short summary (with how the system works today), terms, why-it-works, endpoints, server behaviour, client state, assumptions, request wrapper, run-time steps, build and rollout, open questions.
Moved build-time items (index, migration, purge table) out of the run-time steps into a separate Build and rollout section; removed the server step numbers so run-time steps are 1 to 9.
Merged the three apply rules (page upsert, feed rule, incremental rule) into one defined term, the apply rule, and removed repeats of it in steps.
Merged the long core-idea explanation and the two deletion paragraphs into one short section on why the watermark is safe.
Added a terms list defining change_seq, watermark, drain, generation, swap, tombstone, apply rule and wrapper; defined each download_status value in one list.
Moved the in-memory sync-running flag out of step 4 into the state section so it is said once.
Merged the old step 7 (pause) wording and resume logic so step numbering became: trigger, begin, pages, pause, resume, drain and swap, incremental, resync, stale watermark.
Folded the repeated 'inactive generation is harmless' notes from the generation paragraph, step 5 and step 9 into step 6 item 5 and step 2.
Replaced references to codes like A-numbers' neighbours and the old step 11/12 with step names where possible; kept A1 to A4 as listed assumptions.

Kept every brief and first-version fact (sizes, 800 pages, gzip, 500/1000 limits, Wi-Fi rule, 15 minutes, 7 days, 5 attempts with 2/4/8/16 s waits, 1 GB disk check, 6-day stale limit, A1 to A4, open question and other open items).
holes: Q1: The core idea says rows become visible in change_seq order because it is assigned at commit. What actually assigns change_seq at commit, and what happens to two transactions that commit at nearly the same moment? (author: The brief states that change_seq comes from one global increasing sequence and is assigned at commit so rows become visible in change_seq order. I do not know the mechanism, and I will not invent one. If two transactions commit together, the guarantee means they are ordered and visible in that order. The plan relies on the guarantee, and I added an open item to confirm it with the Catalogue team.)
